summary: LUNARSELENE is a platform that helps explore and compare potential landing sites on the Moon, with a focus on the lunar South Pole. It uses NASA's SPICE data to study sunlight, solar position, and Earth's visibility at different locations over time. The results are presented through interactive dashboards, charts, timelines, and 3D visualizations, making it easier to understand the conditions that could affect future lunar missions.
details:
LUNARSELENE Project Details

LUNARSELENE is a lunar mission planning platform that helps users explore potential landing sites near the Moon’s south pole and understand the environmental conditions at those locations. The idea behind the project is to bring important mission-planning information together in one interactive dashboard instead of having to examine different datasets and calculations separately.

The platform allows users to select candidate landing locations, including the Shackleton Crater region, choose a mission date and time, and explore the conditions at that location. It uses NASA NAIF SPICE ephemeris data to calculate the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the selected lunar site. Based on these calculations, users can examine solar elevation, cumulative sunlight duration, Earth elevation and geometric direct-to-Earth visibility over a seven-day evaluation period. The results are displayed through a 3D lunar globe, mission metric cards, timelines and visual comparisons between two mission scenarios.

One of the main benefits of LUNARSELENE is that it makes lunar environmental data easier to understand and explore. Instead of looking at raw astronomical data, users can interact with a visual representation of the Moon and see how mission conditions change depending on the selected location and time. The scenario comparison feature also makes it easier to examine different mission possibilities and understand how environmental conditions could influence landing-site selection and mission planning.

Our intended impact is to support better-informed planning for future lunar exploration, especially around the lunar south pole, where sunlight availability and communication opportunities are important considerations. We hope the platform can make scientific data more accessible to students, researchers and anyone interested in lunar exploration.

We developed the frontend using React, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS. Three.js was used for the interactive 3D lunar visualization, while Recharts was used for data visualizations. The backend was developed using Python and FastAPI, with SpiceyPy providing access to NASA SPICE calculations. We used NASA NAIF SPICE kernels, including DE421, to obtain the astronomical data used by the platform. GitHub was used for version control, and Render was used to deploy the frontend and backend.

What makes LUNARSELENE creative is the way it combines astronomical calculations, 3D visualization and mission scenario comparison into a single interactive experience. Rather than presenting scientific information as a collection of numbers, we wanted users to be able to explore a lunar location, change mission parameters and immediately see the resulting calculations in context.

During development, our team considered several factors, including the location of candidate landing sites, mission date and time, sunlight availability, the geometric visibility of Earth, the reliability of the underlying astronomical data and the clarity of the user interface. We also considered the importance of distinguishing actual calculated results from unavailable or estimated information. For example, our current Earth visibility calculations are geometric and do not yet account for terrain obstructions or guarantee an actual communication link. These limitations are important when interpreting the results.

Overall, LUNARSELENE is our attempt to make lunar mission planning more visual, understandable and accessible while using real astronomical data to explore some of the challenges involved in future Moon missions!!
